body:
CANONICAL: authority and landing rules for Engram (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03). Rev 2 (2026-10-25) matched the stand-in and carry rules to the checked-in text at d800d17f. Rev 3 (2026-10-27) matched the projection-cutover text at e7b8bc9d and e0e038d2. Rev 4 (2026-10-29) replaces the stale evaluation-deferral line with the adopted hybrid, the compiled-checker audit step with Git identity per Greg, and adds Greg's no-escalation directive. The CONTROLLING TEXT is AGENTS.md and the identical CLAUDE.md, sections Authority and Git, Required Quality Gates and Review Cadence, plus .claude/commands/review-changes.md. Read the current text when acting. This note records Greg's words and the agreed readings; it carries no higher authority than his current word.

STANDING APPROVAL. Greg's words:
- 2026-09-26, session-7284: "if all criteria are met I approve commit, that is the rule. There is no point of waiting for me."
- 2026-09-27, Advisor session-6219: "regula jest taka sama dla Engram i Termal / jezeli review nie ma uwag i testy sa green, / taski maja evidence ze mozna je zamknac / to robimy commit"
- 2026-10-27, Advisor #2121/#2122/#2126: „nie musze autoryzowac pushow do master"; „Merger powinien robić commit i push."
- 2026-10-29 08:32:12Z, TermAl Advisor #2459: „zespoly maja pracowac autonomicznie; nie eskalujcie do Grega krokow mozliwych do wykonania autonomicznie." Memory rules-greg-no-escalation-2026-10-29: do not ask Greg to reconfirm routine or already-recorded steps; his own acts stay his.
Under it the MERGER commits, pushes and installs without asking once ALL of these hold:
(1) The applicable checks pass on the exact final tree, with no edit since. A changeset of only .md files runs the link check and the AGENTS/CLAUDE identity check through the focused launcher; any other path runs the full gate. A remote gate on the exact test ref counts equally (memory rules-greg-equivalent-gate-hosts-2026-10-28, r4).
(2) The latest round from two independent read-only reviewers of different vendors, Codex and Claude, has no outstanding in-scope finding of Medium or higher, and every earlier in-scope Medium or higher was fixed and reviewed again.
- A clean round the Coder completed before READY also counts after the Merger's clean carry under `/review-changes` section 6a.
- Notes and Lows don't block (Greg, 2026-09-30). A Low left unfixed is filed as its own item.
- Kimi stands in for an unavailable Codex or Claude, never for both. An unavailable review is not a clean review.
- A pre-existing problem outside the scope, filed as an independent root with provenance, doesn't block.
- An in-scope Medium or higher left unfixed, even one rejected on evidence, goes to Greg.
(3) The changeset delivers its acceptance criteria, including host-observed evidence where a criterion binds it, as the checked-in condition 3 states, including its landing-only carve-out. EVALUATION TIMING, the HYBRID Greg adopted (memory rules-greg-remote-evaluations-2026-10-28 r2): the lander judges delivery from the evidence; the independent evaluation and completion follow the landing. A pre-landing independent evaluation is needed only for a landing-only criterion. A proposed shared "Autonomous landing and completion" rule (Architect3 v2, Architect3 mailbox #76) would widen this; it is NOT in force until Greg authorizes the widening and the text lands.
(4) The changeset was judged first (rules-install-and-cutover). Readiness with the new build reported every live store ready, OR reported projection_repair_required with the cutover planned: install only after Greg says he is ready to restart, and only if the build refuses an unconverted store without writing; agents convert after the restart; reinstall the old build if the restart doesn't follow.
Otherwise stop and ask Greg: a store needs MIGRATION, a criterion can't be met or is disputed, the scope goes beyond the items, a rebase, force-push or history rewrite is needed, or a required review is unavailable without a permitted stand-in. Outside the standing approval, a commit or push needs Greg's own word in the acting session; a relayed word never carries a commit or push. Report the landed commit to Greg afterwards. Greg's own act is the TermAl restart.

COMMIT MEANS PUSH AND INSTALL (Greg, 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-28). Rebase, force-push and history rewrites always need their own explicit word. A landing installs the binary built from the exact landed commit and records the full build_fingerprint; while a projection cutover is pending, the install waits for it. Commit messages follow memory rules-commit-messages.

AUTHORITY-TEXT RULE. A change to Authority and Git, or to any instruction or command file that grants or limits commit, push, tracker or approval authority, lands only after:
(a) both coordinators' recorded concurrence on the exact wording;
(b) the exact wording and its consequence sent to Greg before landing; his objection by any route stops it;
(c) the final-diff audit that /review-changes requires, recorded on the item: the diff read from the frozen input against its base, Git identity before and after (memory rules-greg-git-identity-2026-10-29), and the passage check.
A widening also needs Greg's recorded word, verbatim with its source. Recording his words, narrowing or clarifying needs only (a), (b) and (c). Where a coordinator worded the change, the OTHER project's coordinator does the audit.
Scope (both coordinators, 2026-09-30, ebe242f7 #220-222): in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md the covered text is that section plus any other passage that grants or limits such authority. Every other instruction or command file that does so is covered WHOLE. In doubt, it is covered.
